industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with a price trigger and an event trigger; conviction medium. Gaztransport & Technigaz (GTT-FR) is a monopoly licensor riding a demand inflection the market has already paid for: at EUR 213.0 (2026-10-05) the modal total shareholder return is about 12.1 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.1 percent a year over three years, against the framework's 20 percent bar. The park rule does not bind (management B, business quality A, predictability A, trackability B); the case is parked on return, not on quality. Progress to Early-Stage if the shares reach about EUR 192 on an unchanged earnings path (the eighteen-month modal case clears the bar there), or if the 2027 LNG carrier order intake runs at or above 2026's pace by mid-2027, which would move the re-rating branch from possible to probable and make the case a B at a higher price. Reverse to bearish if a standard LNG carrier is ordered on a non-GTT containment system or if 2027 intake falls below 30 units.
case: - The thesis: a demand inflection seen from its second leg, in a monopoly licensor whose earnings follow its customers' order book with a two-to-three-year lag. LNG carrier orders collapsed in 2025 and recovered hard in 2026 (65 in H1 2026 against 17); the backlog rose to EUR 1.85 billion, dated by year; management raised the ten-year outlook to about 550 carriers. Because about half of each licence is recognised 24 to 36 months after the order, FY2026 is the trough (revenue guided down 4 percent, earnings per share about flat) and FY2027 and FY2028 are the recovery years (earnings per share up about 8 and 13 percent on our path to EUR 12.4 and EUR 14.0).

- The change is external, sector-level and dated: 107 to 116 MTPA sanctioned, 250 vessels needed over two to three years, about 200 steam-turbine carriers due for replacement, seaborne LNG trade projected at 4 to 5 percent a year 2026 to 2029. Demand (KQ 1, RA 1, E 1, BB 1) is A on the framework's full 'Demand Inflection' test; the company's own cycle (KQ 6) is B, trough in revenue, turning in orders. Competition, disruption, regulation, supply and macro are each C, mild headwinds or mixed: Hanwha's Type B fuel tanks on six container ships (September 2026), HD Hyundai Samho's three-tank hull, the final April 2023 Korean antitrust ruling permitting unbundling on request (none requested), Korean yard labour down 44 percent 2014 to 2024, Hormuz disruption deferring the glut by about two years.

- The internal change is consolidation, not transformation (RA 2, E 1, BB 1 at B): an external chief executive since January 2026, the One GTT structure, the Elogen cut, the Danelec integration, the outlook raised earlier than the market expected; the core licence business and its capital allocation (80 percent payout, no buyback) are unchanged.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the bull case at full force (Bernstein, EUR 245): the backlog inflection is happening now; 2028 to 2031 consensus upgrades follow; free cash flow runs about EUR 400 million a year for six years; a lower cost of capital justifies a re-rating. In its strongest form GTT is a royalty compounder, not a cyclical: the 550-carrier outlook with 250 tied to sanctioned projects and 200 steam-turbine replacements makes the order book a floor, not a wave; FY2029 to FY2031 are covered by orders not yet in a three-broker consensus; the Marine leg makes a tenth of revenue recurring; net cash grows under an 80 percent payout; terminal-value risk is pushed to 2045 or beyond; at 16 times with a 5 percent free-cash-flow yield and a monopoly margin the shares deserve the ten-year 75th percentile. On that reading the return is 20 to 27 percent a year (bull earnings path at 16.0 to 17.9 times) and the case is an A thesis bought at a fair price. Evidence for it: the 2026 orders, the raised outlook, the dated backlog, three years of beats, the Petronas and Petrobras fleet wins, the revision series. Our concessions: the direction of every one of those facts; our FY2029 of EUR 14.8 is more likely too low than too high given 56 LNG carriers in one half-year; the Marine leg has started well. Why we hold: the 550 outlook is 55 carriers a year on average, below the 2026 run-rate, so the wave shape is management's own; the orderbook-to-fleet ratio at a decade high is the fact the bull case has to explain away; the re-rating to 17.9 times needs a 2027 intake we judge possible, not probable; the price has already paid the first leg. We would be wrong against this if 2027 intake exceeds 100 carriers.

- At Building Block 2, the false-friend reading: the backlog masks structural licensing erosion as unbundling, patent expiry, three-tank hulls and royalty pushback hollow out the service and royalty base slowly, so the foundations decay under a record order book. Every mechanism is real and the direction of customer pressure is one way. We hold because the base rate is zero (no unbundling request in over three years; no Type B order for a standard carrier in 2025; the royalty held at about 5 percent through the lull) and the saving on offer is about 3 to 5 percent of vessel cost against an unproven containment risk on a USD 240 million asset; erosion is possible over ten years, not probable over three.
triggers: - The 2027 LNG carrier order intake: probable above 50, possible above 100, possible below 30. Above 100 by mid-2027 moves the re-rating branch to probable and makes the case a B at a higher price (progress); below 30 is the research's own invalidation, taking the three-year earnings path down about 15 percent and the multiple toward 12.9 times (reverse to bearish); alarm below 50.

- The price: at about EUR 192 on an unchanged earnings path the eighteen-month modal case clears the 20 percent bar (progress to Early-Stage); a move to 14.7 times without an earnings cut is the entry wanted; below 12.9 times on unchanged earnings invalidates the return case.

- The moat: one standard LNG carrier ordered on a non-GTT containment system (Type B aluminium, KC-2, Solidus) is the alarm and a reverse-to-bearish trigger; newbuild share below 90 percent for two quarters invalidates.

- The post-2028 cycle: orderbook-to-fleet above 40 percent is the alarm; 2028 intake below 30 invalidates; a rapid Middle East settlement would reverse the fleet tightness and the deferred glut together.

- Unbundling: a first shipyard request under the Korean ruling is the alarm; a request plus a disclosed fee cut invalidates; the licence-versus-technical-assistance fee split is undisclosed, so the magnitude is unknown.
- Backlog recognition: FY2027 revenue below EUR 790 million is the alarm; a reported material milestone delay or cancellation invalidates; the next results are 2027-02-24 with FY2027 guidance.
